    Periodic localization of the mesh derivative #

    Proposition 5.1 (prop:periodic-localization, mesh-deformations.tex).

    A correction column has at most two entries (column_eq). On a row (x, w) with w = p a and a : y → x, the column (σ a, p) connects the row to its rotation (y, (σ σ a) p) when y is nonprojective, and has the row as its only entry when y is projective. Rotating moves every vertex of the path one step to the right and brings in the translate of the vertex before the last one; after d rotations a row is translated by τ. A row with a vertex that is not τ-periodic therefore reaches a one-entry column after finitely many rotations, and elimination from that end puts it in the image of D_m (row_mem_imageD_of_not_periodic).

    The counting is organized by the potential d·δ(v_i) + (d - 1 - i), minimized over the positions i < d of the path, where δ(v) is the number of times τ can be applied to v. One rotation lowers it by exactly one.
